A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Conformal Prediction as Bayesian Quadrature. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic binomial simulations and MS-COCO experiments in Section 5, Tables 1–2, and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 reports the retained experimental tasks with updated results and adds original heteroskedastic regression simulations in Section 5.2 and Table 2.

M1.justification: The quantile-function construction, Dirichlet-weighted loss bound, and posterior-probability threshold selection remain unchanged. The revised Figure 1 explains existing components rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds heteroskedastic regression with X uniform on [0,4] and Y conditional on X normally distributed with variance X squared. Evaluating prediction-interval miscoverage extends task coverage beyond the retained synthetic binomial losses and MS-COCO multilabel classification.

E2.justification: RCPS with a Hoeffding upper confidence bound is added to the existing binomial comparison in Table 1; v1 evaluated it only on MS-COCO. The MS-COCO comparator set is unchanged, and the new regression table identifies split conformal prediction and CRC together.

E3.justification: The new regression experiment introduces 200 calibration samples, symmetric prediction intervals, a miscoverage target of 0.1, and mean interval length as an evaluation measure. The stated binomial settings, MS-COCO split sizes, and Monte Carlo budget for existing experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The decision-rule histograms and analysis of the loss-bound distribution at three threshold values remain unchanged in Figures 3–4. The new heteroskedastic experiment adds task evaluation, without a separate ablation, sensitivity sweep, or distribution-shift analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10,000 trials and use 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals for synthetic failure frequencies. The new regression table follows this existing practice; changed confidence-interval endpoints are result updates, not changes to statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes binomial failure frequencies from 20.92% to 21.20% for CRC and 0.11% to 0.03% for the proposed method, adding RCPS at 0%. MS-COCO frequencies change from 43.76% to 45.05% for CRC and 5.11% to 5.43% for the proposed method; CRC set size changes from 2.93 to 2.92. New regression results report failure frequencies of 46.19%, 0%, and 3.42%, with interval lengths 7.99, 14.29, and 9.50 for CRC, RCPS, and the proposed method, respectively.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, propositions, theorems, and proofs in the main text and Appendices A–B are unchanged mathematically. Appendix B.2 corrects the printed 'infty' to the infinity symbol without changing the assumption or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a Bayesian quadrature interpretation, recovery of split conformal prediction and CRC, and distributional loss guarantees without specifying a particular prior.

C2.justification: Section 6 explicitly distinguishes data-conditional from input-conditional guarantees and expands the explanation of eliminating the prior. It also strengthens the empirical interpretation to claim compliance with the failure-rate limit, although Table 3 reports 5.43% against the stated 5% target. The existing independence and bounded-loss limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a GitHub code-access link and documents the generation process and settings for the added regression experiment. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: v2 adds Barber et al. (2021) and Gibbs et al. (2024) when distinguishing its guarantees from input-conditional inference. It removes the Jaynes (1983) quotation and reference. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: the synthetic subsection is renamed, a regression subsection and Impact Statement are added, and the Discussion is expanded while its opening quotation is removed. There are also wording, typography, acknowledgement, and publication-header edits; the overall organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to explain unknown quantile levels and the upper-bounding construction. v2 adds the regression results table, expands Table 1 with RCPS, and relocates the MS-COCO table and Figure 4. Figures 2–4 retain their graphical content, and the document keeps its existing layout style.

improvement.justification: The added regression evaluation and binomial RCPS comparison modestly strengthen the evidence, while the revised schematic, conditioning explanation, and code link improve clarity and reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by the stronger, unsupported statement that the failure-rate limit is not exceeded: v2's MS-COCO table reports 5.43% against a 5% target. The unchanged method and proofs support a limited overall improvement.
